## Doob's Submartingale Inequality

*Doob's martingale inequality*, also known as Kolmogorov's submartingale
inequality, gives a bound on the probability that a submartingale exceeds a
given value over a given interval of time. Informally, **the expected value of
the process at some final time controls the probability that a sample path
reaches above any particular value beforehand**.

The proof uses very direct reasoning, so it does not require any restrictive
assumptions on the underlying filtration or on the process itself. In the
continuous-time setting, right-continuity (or left-continuity) of the sample
paths is required, but only so that the supremum of a sample path equals the
supremum over a countable dense subset of times.

:::{.theorem data-title="Doob's Submartingale Inequality"}

Suppose that $(X_n, \mathcal{F}_n)_{n\ge 0}$ is a
[[martingale-theory|submartingale]]. Then for every $\lambda>0$ and $n\ge 0$,
$$
\lambda\,\mathbb{P}\left( \max_{0\le k\le n}X_k \ge \lambda \right)
\le \mathbb{E}\left[ X_n \mathbb{1}_{\{ \max_{0\le k\le n}X_k \ge \lambda \}} \right]
\le \mathbb{E}[X_n^+].
$$

:::

After rearranging, the result is similar in form to the
[[markov-inequality]],
$$
\mathbb{P}\left( \max_{0\le k\le n}X_k \ge \lambda \right)
\le \frac{\mathbb{E}[X_n^+]}{\lambda}.
$$

`\begin{proof}`
We define a [[stopping-times|stopping time]] 
$$
\tau:=\inf\{k \geq 0:X_{k}\geq \lambda\}
$$
(where $\tau= +\infty$ is $X_{k}<\lambda$ for all $k \geq 0$). Furthermore, we
define event
$$
A:=\{ \max_{0\leq k\leq n}X_{k}\geq \lambda \}=\{ \tau\leq n \}\in\mathcal{F}_{\tau \wedge n}\subseteq \mathcal{F}_{\tau}.
$$
Then, for every $k=0,1,\dots,n$ we have
$A\subset \{ \tau=k \}\in \mathcal{F}_{k}$ and also
$A \cap \{ \tau\geq n+1 \}\in \mathcal{F}_{n}$. This implies
$$
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}[X_{\tau \wedge n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{A}] & = \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{k=0}^\infty X_{\tau \wedge n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{A\cap \{ \tau=k \}} \right] =\mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{k=0}^\infty X_{k}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{A\cap \{ \tau=k \}}+X_{n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{A \cap \{ \tau \geq n+1 \}} \right]  \\
& \leq  \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{k=0}^n X_{n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{A\cap \{ \tau=k \}}+X_{n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{A\cap \{ \tau \geq n+1 \}} \right]=\mathbb{E}[X_{n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{A}],
\end{align}
$$
where the inequality follows from the submartingale property. Using this
inequality, since $X_{\tau}\geq \lambda$ on the set $A$, we obtain
$$
\begin{align}
\lambda \cdot \mathbb{P}\left( \max_{0\leq k\leq n} X_{k}\geq \lambda \right) & = \lambda \cdot \mathbb{P}(A) = \mathbb{E}[\lambda \mathbb{1}_{A}]\leq \mathbb{E}[X_{\tau}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{A}]=\mathbb{E}[X_{\tau \wedge n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{\tau\leq  n}]  \\
& \leq \mathbb{E}[X_{n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{\tau \leq  n}] = \mathbb{E}[X_{n}\cdot \mathbb{1}_{\max_{0\leq k\leq n}(X_{k})\geq  \lambda}]\leq  \mathbb{E}[X_{n}^+].
\end{align}
$$
`\end{proof}`

## Further Maximal Inequalities

:::{.theorem data-title="Doob's Maximal Inequalities"}

Let $(X_n, \mathcal{F}_n)$ be a submartingale. Then

1. **$L^p$ inequality:** for $p>1$,
   $$
   \mathbb{E}\left[ \left( \max_{0\le m\le n}X_m^+ \right)^p \right]
   \le \left( \frac{p}{p-1} \right)^p \mathbb{E}\left[ (X_n^+)^p \right].
   $$
2. **Minimal inequality:** for $\lambda>0$,
   $$
   \lambda\,\mathbb{P}\left( \min_{0\le m\le n}X_m \le -\lambda \right)
   \le \mathbb{E}[X_n^+] - \mathbb{E}[X_0].
   $$
3. **Doob-Kolmogorov inequality:** if $(X_n, \mathcal{F}_n)$ is a martingale
   with $\mathbb{E}[X_n^2]<\infty$ for all $n$, then for $\lambda>0$
   $$
   \mathbb{P}\left( \max_{0\le m\le n}|X_m| \ge \lambda \right)
   \le \frac{\mathbb{E}[X_n^2]}{\lambda^2}.
   $$

:::

`\begin{proof}`
For (3), $X_n^2$ is a submartingale by Jensen's inequality (see
[[martingale-theory]]), so applying the submartingale inequality to $X_n^2$
with level $\lambda^2$ gives
$$
\lambda^2\,\mathbb{P}\left( \max_{0\le m\le n}X_m^2 \ge \lambda^2 \right)
\le \mathbb{E}[X_n^2].
$$
For (1) and (2) see
[[files-notes-pstat213bc-lecture-notes-raya-pdf|PSTAT213BC Lecture Notes (Raya), page 102]].
`\end{proof}`

## Applications

- [[kolmogorovs-maximal-inequality-for-sums|Kolmogorov's maximal inequality
  for sums]] follows from the Doob-Kolmogorov inequality applied to
  $S_n - \mathbb{E}S_n$.
- The inequalities are used to prove the [[martingale-convergence-theorems]].
